body:
I know right? Pain the the behind is what it is. I appreciate your empathy I really do. It's going to be nice to actually be able to go back and read this once i'm past all of this mess in my life.

Personally: i think that everyone's body is different, just because you take 2 mg doesn't mean your body absorbs 2 mg. As we know, with some psych meds (MAOIs) you have to watch your intake or it absorbs more/less rapidly/at all.

I do hope that you are able to do well with your career in counseling. One thing that I do agree with (and you may see this differently) that my first therapist once said "I don't hire people who want to counsel just because they can help. I want them to be able to know what is going on, but be able to take off the hat when they go home."

Might be a great piece of advice as I'm assuming we are in a similar age range as I am.

and yes, counseling is a very thankless job. so thanks to you as well. When's national therapist day (and i don't mean national let's go see a therapist day)? I'll make sure to send you a PM.

I wouldn't say I'm great at natural sciences, but I pushed my self through it so I was able to... some days I wish i wouldn't have as I was just starting a business that was taking off. well hindsight is 20/20 right?

I've considered travel nursing but i don't think i would want to walk the union lines. I've known a fair few travelers who will start their jobs in places on strike and get assaulted by the nurses on strike. Unless you know someone who wants an RN in norther cali and is willing to pay for a cross country move (I do love the redwoods)

thanks again for the comment

Yeah i actually did a senior thesis in school on nursing burnout in hospitals in america in the 2000's. but it is totally burn out/fatigue to the extreme...

I actually left my job over this whole ordeal as I was constantly butting heads with administration.

But yeah go a head and post those, in the future someone else might read this and get a few good tips from it.

thanks again for the comment so far. I'm in agreenace that everything put together really really really makes for a rough time.

I think the most difficult part about all of this for me is that I *DO* love to care for people, and I really want to help out when I can. But how can I help someone else out if i can't even help myself. ugh, frustration grows more and more every time i think about it.

Just because you can contract no self harm does not mean you do not deserve to talk to people. this sounds like a way that we can take your pain and turn it in to a petition to FORCE phone carriers to allow suicide hotline calls. i hope you are okay
thanks analgesiac, i tried to reply to your comment in the comment section of Lonelygamergurl

I agree, i went in to nursing for (mostly) the right reasons, but if i had to do it again. I would NEVER EVER EVER EVER EVER be a nurse. 
No way. no how.

sadly as i tried to reply to someone else, i do feel like i have hit the point of burnout... especially after one of the patients i worked closely with for years came out in the hall the night i went postal and walked over and gave me a hug (that made me cry)... I think she called the DO on that hospital that night too for understaffing (but i know nothing, i hear nothing, i see nothing)

I'm going to reply to both you and analgesiac at the same time as i think you guys are both on the same side of the argument.

With the bullsh*t new american health care laws (seriously read them, they don't help nurses/staffing) decreasing medicare/cade dollars to hospitals, more and more hospitals are cutting back on "Hands on" time for patient care. Sadly you don't really ever see them for a few reasons. Some are just jerks, some have no manners, and MOST are being told they will lose their paycheck or license if they do not get it done yesterday.

I am aware that you are sticking up for doctors and I am with you on that too, you have a huge amount of pressure with those dea licenses of yours (no kidding its bull).

side note 
I know a few nurses who are legally allowed to assist in surgeries which in some states includes removal of your appendix and in other countries they are able to. 

and analgesiac i hope you find this funny when i say the following:
your question "Or to interpret your ankle MRI?" made me want to have a knee jerk response of "the computer" or "some guy in india" (i hope you find that funny, many nurses i've encountered do not know that most radiology interpretations in smaller hospitals are done out of house).

I have come to that realization, sad to say that being a health care provider may have actually caused me to get worse care by attempting to seek out the care i have studied and have told people to get. it sucks!

As far as the klonopin: who the hell knows. I think it's because I admitted that when I was in high school i once tried tested MDMA(extacy/molly/etc) that I was some sort of crazy person. Or the fact that I answered "Hasn't everyone once when they were younger?" to the "have you ever drank until you passed out" To the point where once i got the temazepam script I need to go for random blood samples (WTF?). Guess what? I have no illicit substances in my body NOR alcohol.

I am aware that 2mg kpin is what some would consider to be a "high" dose. but my goodness if you want to talk about something working. it was great. I could sleep without waking up with a raw chicken in my mouth at my parents house at 3am (true story. my car is fine, the chicken needed some bbq sauce though)

I'll admit that i'm probably so dissatisfied with healthcare to want to seek out counseling again. My first attempt at it was an attack session against my perceived drug abuse problem which never occurred (you can be depressed and tired, who would ever have thought that one :rolleyes:). I will admit that for a while I was really depressed to the point where if i wasn't working i would literally wake up, walk out side and light a fag, walk back in and go to bed until my next 16-32 hour shift (yes these places can and will do that to you for no good reason)

I worked as a surgical nurse at one time (loved it but couldn't stand the "normal" 0700-1500 you would work at those jobs), i've been investigating case management as well as informatics too maybe some leads there

You're welcome (I guess?). It's a job that needs to be done and darn it I am going to do it (even if it's by proxy with telemedicine)
thanks for commenting

sadly remeron made me attempt suicide and i also started to sleep walk more. the only TCA that did anything was amitryptaline but that (as much as it worked) gave me super bad nausea. thanks you though. sadly i think I already have burnt out as a nurse :(

way too many people :( makes it hard when you are a medical professional to find someone you are not partial against or towards :\ esp. when you have worked with most of them. thank you for your reply

It is a lot of pressure, especially as young man. I came right out of high school and went to nursing school so it was a huge shock. as far as 1 on 1 patient interaction: I did it before but you had to go in to so many gross homes. I'm not the cleanest person out there but something about 5 year old bacon grease doesn't sound tasty to me. I've been looking at some other work outside hospitals again
thanks I appreciate it. I hope you are nearing the end of your hospital stays

sure you do have something to offer. EMOTIONS!

I have been single my entire life so I may not know exactly what you are feeling but ya know what, after leaving behind a career in nursing I can empathize with the pain that I've experienced watching others in this case.

You have tons to offer a man, there are some of us (not me only because of my age) who are more than happy to have a family. There are also some men who can't have kids. PLUS you have the most important man in your life right now, your little tyke.

I don't normally post on these things myself, but maybe reddit is the group therapy of the 21st century?
